 COLUMBIA — Polls have closed across South Carolina in the 2026 Midterm elections.
 On the federal side, Midlands residents are choosing who to send to represent their interests in the U.S. House of Representatives in both District 2 and District 6.
 The Associated Press called the election in District 6 for Incumbent Jim Clyburn at 8:37 p.m. Clyburn (D-Columbia) has held his seat representing South Carolina’s sixth congressional district since he was elected in 1992. District 6 stretches all the way from Columbia down to Charleston, comprising most of the state’s majority-Black precincts. Clyburn was up against Republican challenger John Peterson.
 In District Two, incumbent Joe Wilson (R-West Columbia) is seeking his 14th term representing Lexington County and parts of Richland County, out to Aiken. He’s facing off against two challengers — Democrat Zyon Khalifa, and Workers Party candidate Dayna Alane Smith.
 There are also 22 seats touching Lexington and Richland County in the state House of Representatives up for grabs, including one featuring Micah Caskey (R-West Columbia), who was chosen as the new house majority leader in September. Preliminary results have him losing the contest with Democrat Joe Madge by 101 votes, but the margin falls within the mark for a state-required recount.
 We’re also tracking local races in Lexington and Richland counties, including school board elections.
 Check back here for the statehouse and federal results, which will be updated as votes roll in.
